## Core Claims (3 conditions)

1. **Complexity-Dependent Reformulation Advantage**: Binary pass/fail classification and execution output generation (CWM-style) achieve equivalent accuracy on simple function-level code (4B: F1 diff 0.9pp), but classification scales better with model size (8B 3-seed mean accuracy gap=2.43pp; seed42: 2.81pp, cls 90.48% vs cwm 87.67%) and to repo-level complexity where CWM failure modes—token-budget exhaustion and string-value prediction errors—dominate. We empirically show: (a) per-test advantage concentrates in instances with multiple FAIL_TO_PASS tests (31% of SWE-bench Verified); (b) PASS_TO_PASS regression detection provides signal only when regression rate exceeds ~10%; (c) block-correlated prediction errors amplify per-test advantage through reduced effective degrees of freedom. ## Story Spine

**Problem**: Test-time scaling for code repair requires ranking candidate patches, but verification paradigms face a granularity-cost tradeoff. Full execution costs ~$1-3 and minutes per candidate. Execution-free alternatives like SWE-RM predict trajectory-level binary correctness at low cost but provide only coarse signals that cannot distinguish between candidates failing on different test subsets.

**Existing approaches & gaps**: Code World Models (Self-Execution Simulation, CWM) predict execution outputs but suffer from token-budget exhaustion and string-value prediction failures. SWE-RM achieves strong trajectory-level scoring but loses per-test diagnostic information. No work studies per-test binary classification as a dedicated verification formulation, or compares classification vs generation formulations for code execution simulation at controlled model sizes.

**Our framing**: We reformulate execution simulation from an open-ended generation task (predict execution trace/output) to a closed-form classification task (predict binary pass/fail per test). On simple function-level code, both formulations achieve equivalent accuracy (~87% F1), because short execution outputs do not trigger CWM failure modes. However, on repo-level code with long execution traces and complex outputs, classification sidesteps token-budget exhaustion and string-value prediction errors, yielding a complexity-dependent advantage. (Downstream re-repair experiment is stretch goal; if not completed, frame as future work.)

Mitigation: frame as (a) probing LLM code semantic reasoning capabilities through per-test prediction, and (b) a general NLP methodology insight about classification vs generation formulations applicable beyond code.

3. **Function-level to repo-level gap**: Function-level results show classification ≈ generation. Repo-level extension is now CRITICAL (not optional) to demonstrate the complexity-dependent advantage. Requires SWE-bench Docker infrastructure. If repo-level also shows no advantage, paper pivots to efficiency framing (same accuracy, lower inference cost) + oracle characterization.
